rules: The box is a square of size by size; glyph fills the box without distortion and is painted in the current content color, so the host decides the color.

glyph is a vector drawing supplied by the application, following the reference icon set's conventions (Phosphor: a square grid, the drawing inset 1/8 of the box on each side); hosts rely on that inset for optical spacing.
Without label the icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; with label it is an image whose accessible name is label.
The box keeps its size in a flexible layout: it neither shrinks nor stretches, and it does not change with density.
The icon has no interaction, no state and no color of its own; a glyph is one color (strokes belong to the drawing, not to the component).
When placed in a host slot that defines an icon size (a Button's leading or trailing slot), the host's size applies instead of the size option.
